note: Hand-written. Play is what you can do — lessons, pools, courts, gyms and group runs; Trails are hikes and rides; Watch is where the teams play, with dated fixtures in events.json. Researched, not visited.

items.title: The Dish loop
items.area: Stanford Avenue trailhead · 3.7 mi loop · about 530 ft up
items.why: A 3.7-mile paved loop over the Stanford foothills past a 150-foot radio telescope, with views across the whole Bay. It climbs more than it looks (about 530 feet). There is almost no shade and very little parking, so go early and bring water. The gates open and close with the daylight, and the times change by month.
items.source: AllTrails; Destination Palo Alto; Wikipedia; trailhead confirmed against OpenStreetMap (node/4562251453)
items.hoursFrom: destinationpaloalto.com — the Dish is open sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: Sunrise to sunset

items.title: Pearson-Arastradero Preserve
items.area: Arastradero Road lot · 3.7 mi loop · about 300 ft up · bikes allowed on its wide trails
items.why: The gentlest hike in Palo Alto: open grassland and oak hills a few minutes past 280, with ten miles of trail to choose from. The Arastradero Creek loop goes out along the Juan Bautista de Anza trail and back by Acorn and Meadowlark. It is good for birds, and the loop to do when you want to be walking in twenty minutes. Some trails close after rain.
items.source: POST (Peninsula Open Space Trust); AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/10781180)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset

items.title: Foothills Nature Preserve
items.area: Page Mill Road entrance · 15 miles of trail
items.priceNote: Entry rules and a daily cap — check before you go
items.why: Palo Alto's own mountain park: fifteen miles of trail in the foothills, with Boronda Lake and Vista Hill. From the top of Vista Hill, on a clear day, you can see Hoover Tower, the Dumbarton Bridge, Mount Diablo and Mount Hamilton. It was for Palo Alto residents only for fifty-one years and opened to everyone in December 2020. Visitor numbers are still capped, so check the city's page for the current rules.
items.source: City of Palo Alto; San Francisco Chronicle; Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/6258591)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset

items.title: Windy Hill — Spring Ridge Trail
items.area: Portola Road lot · 5.6 mi · about 1,370 ft up
items.why: The climb the Peninsula knows by sight: the bare green hill above Portola Valley. Go up Spring Ridge Trail from the Portola Road lot to the top, where the whole bay spreads out below. It is steep and open, so go early. For a longer day, make it a 7.5-mile loop down Hamms Gulch through the woods.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; POST; AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/193017)
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset

items.title: Rancho San Antonio — PG&E Trail
items.area: Cristo Rey Drive lots · 4.3 mi loop · about 700 ft up
items.why: The busiest trailhead on the Peninsula, for good reason. There are loops of every length, from an easy walk to Deer Hollow Farm (baby goats in spring) up to eleven-plus miles up the PG&E Trail. The classic is the PG&E, Wildcat and Coyote loop. The one catch is parking: on a summer weekend the lots are full by eight, so arrive before that.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; Hilltromper; AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/296113630)
items.imageSubject: Rancho San Antonio Open Space Preserve
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset

items.title: Purisima Creek Redwoods
items.area: Skyline Boulevard or Purisima Creek Road · 4.8 to 10.5 mi loops
items.why: The nearest proper redwood forest to Palo Alto, on the ocean side of Skyline. The 4.8-mile Grabtown Gulch and Borden Hatch Mill loop goes through second-growth redwoods. The full day is about ten miles down the creek and back up. There is also a quarter-mile flat, wheelchair-accessible path through tall redwoods right off Skyline. It is often in fog, so bring a layer.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; Bay Area Ridge Trail; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/193021)
items.imageSubject: Purisima Creek Redwoods Open Space Preserve
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset

items.title: Mori Point
items.area: Pacifica · 1.7 to 2.6 mi loops
items.why: A short coastal loop over a headland in Pacifica, with the Pacific on three sides. You climb the steep Bootlegger's Steps to the top of the bluff, named for the Prohibition smugglers who landed here. It takes an hour, so it works as a morning before breakfast, or as the walk to end a day on the coast.
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy; AllTrails; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/3923236)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov — the trails are open around the clock, the car parks sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: The trails never close; the car park is open sunrise to sunset

items.title: Tennessee Valley to the beach
items.area: Mill Valley, end of Tennessee Valley Road · 3.4 mi out and back
items.why: An easy, nearly flat walk down a green valley to a small cove beach on the Pacific, 1.7 miles each way. The first half-mile is paved. It is the Marin hike for a slow morning or for anyone who doesn't want to climb. The lot fills fast at weekends, and cars end up parked far down the road.
items.source: AllTrails; Marin County Visitor; road confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/659312700)
items.coordsFrom: osm way/659312700 (end of Tennessee Valley Road)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov — the trails are open around the clock, the car parks sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: The trails never close; the car park is open sunrise to sunset

items.title: Steep Ravine & Matt Davis loop
items.area: Stinson Beach trailhead · about 6.4 mi · about 1,900 ft up
items.why: The best loop on Mount Tamalpais, and a full morning. Go up the Matt Davis Trail from Stinson Beach, through forest and then out onto grassland high above the Pacific. Come down Steep Ravine, past waterfalls and redwoods and down the famous wooden ladder. It climbs about 1,900 feet. Finish in the sea at Stinson.
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy; Bay Area Hiker; AllTrails; trail confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/1442270016)
items.hoursFrom: parks.ca.gov — Mount Tamalpais State Park, 7am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 7am to sunset

items.title: Over the Golden Gate to Sausalito
items.area: From Aquatic Park · about 8 mi · paths, some road, hills at the bridge
items.priceNote: Bike hire from the Wharf; ferry back ~$15
items.why: The classic ride. From Aquatic Park it runs along the water through Fort Mason, the Marina and Crissy Field, climbs to the bridge and crosses it, then drops down into Sausalito. Take the ferry back instead of climbing home. In 2026 that means the Golden Gate Ferry to the Ferry Building, because the Blue & Gold boat to Pier 41 isn't running while its dock is repaired. Bike hire is all along Fisherman's Wharf.
items.source: Blazing Saddles; OurSausalito; Inside Guide to San Francisco Tourism; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/32839638)
items.hoursNote: Bikes may cross the bridge at any hour, through gates at night; the ferry back runs to a timetable

items.title: Golden Gate Park to Ocean Beach
items.area: JFK Promenade from the Conservatory · 3.4 mi each way · car-free, paved
items.priceNote: Free; bike share at the park
items.why: The easy one, and entirely in the city. JFK Drive through Golden Gate Park has been car-free since 2020, made permanent in 2022. Start at the Conservatory of Flowers and roll west past the museums and lakes all the way to the ocean. It is a gentle downhill out and a gentle climb back. Carry on along the Great Highway path by Ocean Beach if you have the legs.
items.source: SF Recreation & Parks; TrailLink; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/30675038)
items.hoursFrom: San Francisco Park Code §3.21 — city parks close from midnight to 5am

items.title: Sawyer Camp Trail
items.area: Crystal Springs Dam · 6 mi each way · paved, car-free
items.why: Six miles of paved, car-free trail along Crystal Springs Reservoir, in the rift valley of the San Andreas Fault. It is halfway between San Francisco and Palo Alto, so it works from either. Halfway along is the Jepson Laurel, more than six hundred years old and the oldest in California. It is shared with walkers and runners, so ride it slow. The county has closed it for storm and culvert repairs before, so check its advisories first.
items.source: County of San Mateo; Wikipedia; trail confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/791183517)
items.hoursFrom: San Mateo County Parks, via Bay Area Hiker
items.hoursNote: Sunrise to sunset

items.title: The Bay Trail: Baylands to Shoreline
items.area: Palo Alto Baylands · flat · gravel and crushed shell, some paved
items.why: Flat riding along the edge of the bay from the Palo Alto Baylands south to Shoreline Park in Mountain View, past salt ponds and marsh, with birds the whole way. The surface is mostly gravel and crushed shell with some paved stretches, so a hybrid is better than a road bike. Shoreline has ten more miles of paths around its lake. The Stevens Creek Trail, paved and off-street, runs inland from there if you want more.
items.source: Bay Trail (MTC); City of Mountain View; MTB Project; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the Baylands interpretive center (on the site already)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset; Shoreline in Mountain View keeps its own
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset

items.title: The Portola Loop
items.area: Sand Hill, Portola and Alpine roads · about 11.5 mi · on the road
items.why: The loop every Peninsula road cyclist knows: Sand Hill, Portola and Alpine roads round Portola Valley, about eleven and a half miles, and packed with riders on weekend mornings. The locals argue about which direction to ride it. It is on the road with cars, with bike lanes most of the way. Ride it early at weekends, when it is mostly other cyclists.
items.source: Palo Alto Bicycles; Bo Crane Books; Strava; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/40187960)
items.hoursFrom: public roads

items.title: Old La Honda climb
items.area: Portola Road, by the stone bridge · 3 mi · just under 8%
items.why: The Peninsula's benchmark climb, for when the loop isn't enough. It is almost exactly three miles at just under eight percent, from the stone bridge off Portola Road up to Skyline, through redwoods and tanoak. The road is narrow and there is some traffic. Come down the way you went up, carefully, or carry on over Skyline for a long day.
items.source: Palo Alto Bicycles; Komoot; road confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/941162598)
items.hoursFrom: public roads

items.title: Giants at Oracle Park
items.area: Oracle Park, 24 Willie Mays Plaza
items.priceNote: Cheap seats in the bleachers; more behind home plate
items.times: MLB, April to late September, most days in season
items.transit: Muni Metro to 2nd & King, or Caltrain to 4th & King
items.why: The best-placed ballpark in America, on the bay at the edge of SoMa. A home run to right field lands in the water of McCovey Cove, where kayakers wait for it. Get bleacher seats and watch the sun go down over the city behind the outfield. Bring a jacket to a night game: it is cold by the fourth inning.
items.source: San Francisco Giants; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Warriors and Valkyries at Chase Center
items.area: Chase Center, Mission Bay
items.priceNote: Warriors are expensive; Valkyries much less so
items.times: Warriors, October to April; Valkyries (WNBA), May to September
items.transit: Muni T Third to the UCSF/Chase Center stop
items.why: The arena in Mission Bay, open since 2019, and home to two teams. The Warriors are the famous ticket. The Valkyries are the better night out: the WNBA's newest team, a sold-out crowd from their first season, and in 2026 one of the best records the league has seen. The waterfront park outside is good before the game.
items.source: Chase Center; SF Standard; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: 49ers at Levi's Stadium
items.area: Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara
items.priceNote: NFL prices; the upper deck is the way in
items.times: NFL, September to January, home games roughly every other Sunday
items.transit: Caltrain to Mountain View, then VTA light rail to Great America
items.why: The 49ers' stadium in Santa Clara, open since 2014, which hosted the Super Bowl in 2016 and again in February 2026. Tailgating in the lots is half the day. Take the train rather than driving: the car parks empty very slowly.
items.source: Levi's Stadium; San Francisco 49ers; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Stanford football at Stanford Stadium
items.area: Stanford Stadium
items.priceNote: Among the cheapest big-stadium tickets in the Bay
items.times: College football, September to November, home Saturdays
items.transit: Caltrain to Palo Alto and walk across campus, or the free Marguerite shuttle
items.why: Big-time college football you can walk to from downtown Palo Alto. The stadium sits in a grove of trees on campus, with the band and a crowd of students. Tickets are easy to get and cheap by the standard of the pros. Make a day of it: lunch on University Avenue, the game, and the Rodin garden on the way home.
items.source: Stanford Athletics; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Lawn bowling in Golden Gate Park
items.area: Bowling Green Drive, Golden Gate Park
items.times: Free lessons Wednesday and Saturday at noon
items.hoursFrom: sflbc.org — free lessons Wednesday and Saturday at noon
items.source: San Francisco Lawn Bowling Club; SF Rec & Park

pairings.text: Conservatory of Flowers, ten minutes east

items.why: The oldest public lawn bowling club in the country, founded in 1901 on a green in Golden Gate Park. Members teach anyone who turns up, free, on Wednesdays and Saturdays at noon, and the lesson takes about an hour. Wear flat-soled shoes, because heels ruin the green. It is gentle, oddly competitive, and nobody you know has done it.

items.title: Swim in the bay at Aquatic Park
items.area: Dolphin Club or South End Rowing Club, Jefferson Street
items.times: Public days Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm, alternating between the two clubs
items.hoursFrom: Dolphin Club and South End Rowing Club — public days Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm
items.source: South End Rowing Club; Dolphin Club; Openwaterpedia

pairings.text: Buena Vista for an Irish coffee after

items.why: Two rowing and swimming clubs from the 1870s share the beach at Aquatic Park, and on public days, Tuesday to Saturday, anyone can pay the day fee and use the sauna, showers and the cove. The water is about 55 to 62°F all year, and the regulars swim in it without wetsuits. Sign the waiver, swim along the buoys inside the breakwater, and sit in the sauna after. Check which club has the public day before you go.

items.title: Learn to surf at Linda Mar
items.area: Pacifica State Beach (Linda Mar), Pacifica
items.priceNote: Group lessons ~$94, board and wetsuit included
items.hoursNote: Lessons are booked for a time, usually mornings, when the wind is lighter
items.source: Nor-Cal Surf Shop; Visit Pacifica

pairings.text: Taco Bell Cantina on the sand, famously
Mori Point for a walk after

items.why: The gentlest surf near the city: a long, sandy cove at the south end of Pacifica, twenty minutes from San Francisco, where the waves break slowly and the bottom is sand. Nor-Cal Surf Shop, across the highway, runs lessons with the board and a thick wetsuit included. Two hours and most people stand up. Mornings are calmer; afternoons bring wind and fog.

items.title: Climbing at Movement Belmont
items.area: The old Belmont Theatre, 100 El Camino Real, Belmont
items.hoursNote: Open early to late every day — check the gym for class times
items.source: Movement Climbing
items.why: A climbing gym inside the old Belmont movie theatre, with walls going up where the screen was: about 19,000 square feet of bouldering and ropes, including real crack climbs. It is half an hour up from Palo Alto and the Peninsula's best place to start. Take the intro class, which teaches you to belay, and you can climb ropes with a friend on your own after that. Movement also has gyms in Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Santa Clara and San Francisco.

items.title: Climbing at Mission Cliffs
items.area: 2295 Harrison Street, the Mission
items.hoursNote: Open early to late every day — check the gym for class times
items.source: Touchstone Climbing
items.why: San Francisco's big old climbing gym, in a warehouse in the Mission: tall roped walls, a bouldering cave and a weights room. It is sociable in the evenings, when half the city's climbers come after work. Book the intro to top-rope class, and after that a day pass is all you need.

items.title: Tennis at the Golden Gate Park courts
items.area: Goldman Tennis Center, east end of Golden Gate Park
items.hoursNote: Courts by reservation — book online; SF residents can book further ahead
items.source: Lifetime Activities; Mission Local
items.why: Seventeen courts in Golden Gate Park, rebuilt in 2021 with a clubhouse and lights for evening play. You book a court by the hour rather than queue for one, which is the whole difference from the free park courts. Clinics and lessons run for every level, if you want to start again properly.

items.title: Baylands Golf Links
items.area: 1875 Embarcadero Road, Palo Alto
items.hoursNote: Tee times from dawn — book online
items.source: City of Palo Alto; Yelp
items.why: Palo Alto's municipal course, rebuilt in 2018 as a links on the edge of the Baylands: no trees, marsh grass, wind off the bay and egrets on the fairways. It is fully public, and the green fees are low for the Peninsula, lower still with a Palo Alto or Bay Area ID. There is a driving range, and the Baylands trails start next door.

items.title: Ride the Hellyer Velodrome
items.area: Hellyer County Park, San Jose
items.priceNote: Beginner sessions and rental bikes — check the schedule
items.hoursNote: Beginner sessions on Saturday mornings
items.source: Hellyer Velodrome; Santa Clara County Parks
items.why: A banked concrete cycling track in a county park in south San Jose, built in 1962. On Saturday mornings supervisors run beginner sessions for people who have never ridden a fixed-gear track bike, and they will lend you one. The first lap on the banking, up near the rail, is frightening and then wonderful.

items.title: Kayak to McCovey Cove
items.area: South Beach Harbor, by Oracle Park
items.hoursNote: Rentals and tours from the harbour — book a slot
items.source: City Kayak; Paddling Magazine
items.why: A kayak rental on the South Beach Harbor docks, ten minutes' paddle from McCovey Cove behind Oracle Park and up Mission Creek past the houseboats. Beginners go on the short guided trips; anyone who has paddled before can rent and go. On Giants days people float in the cove waiting for a home run to land in the water.

items.title: Kayak or paddleboard from Sausalito
items.area: Schoonmaker Point Marina, Sausalito
items.hoursNote: Rentals daily from the marina — mornings are calmest
items.source: Sea Trek; Visit Marin
items.why: Paddle out from a sheltered beach in Sausalito and along Richardson Bay, past the floating houseboats and the harbour seals, with the city across the water. Rentals go by the hour and there is an intro class if you have never been in a kayak. Go in the morning: the wind comes up through the Golden Gate after lunch.

items.title: Rinconada Pool
items.area: 777 Embarcadero Road, Palo Alto
items.hoursFrom: Palo Alto Swim — lap swim weekdays 6am to 4pm, Saturday to 5pm
items.source: Palo Alto Swim; City of Palo Alto
items.why: Palo Alto's outdoor pool in Rinconada Park: a big heated outdoor pool, open for lap swimming from six in the morning. It is the cheapest good exercise in town and the best way to start a hot day. Pay at the desk and share a lane. Check the schedule in winter, when hours shorten.

items.title: November Project
items.area: Fort Mason or Alta Plaza, early mornings
items.times: Monday and Wednesday at 6:29am; Friday hills at the Golden Gate
items.hoursNote: Monday and Wednesday at 6:29am, Fort Mason or Alta Plaza; Friday on the hills — check the group for the week
items.source: November Project; SF Funcheap
items.why: A free, loud, early workout that started in Boston and is now in dozens of cities. In San Francisco the group meets at 6:29 on Monday and Wednesday mornings, at Fort Mason or Alta Plaza, for stairs, hills and bodyweight circuits, and on the hills near the bridge on Fridays. You just show up. Somebody will hug you. It is the fastest way to meet people who run.
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

items.title: Disc golf in Golden Gate Park
items.area: Marx Meadow, western Golden Gate Park
items.priceNote: Free; bring or buy a disc
items.hoursFrom: SF Rec & Park — park hours
items.source: SF Rec & Park; PDGA course directory
items.why: Eighteen holes among the cypress and eucalyptus of western Golden Gate Park, free and open to anyone. It is golf with a frisbee: a par three is a throw between the trees to a chain basket. Any sports shop sells a starter disc for a few dollars. Weekends are busy, so let faster groups through.

items.title: The Crissy Field run
items.area: Marina Green to Fort Point and back
items.hoursFrom: Golden Gate National Recreation Area — open every day
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy

stops.text: Start at the Marina Green, by the yacht harbour
Along the Crissy Field promenade, flat and on the water
Touch the fence at Fort Point, right under the bridge
Turn and run back with the city in front of you

items.why: The best run in San Francisco and one of the flattest: the old airfield along the bay from the Marina to the foot of the Golden Gate. It is four kilometres out on packed gravel, with the bridge getting bigger the whole way, and the tradition is to touch the fence at Fort Point before turning round. Go early before the wind, or at sunset when the bridge goes orange.

items.title: Lake Merced loop
items.area: Lake Merced, south-west San Francisco
items.hoursFrom: SF Rec & Park
items.source: SF Rec & Park
items.why: A paved path all the way round the city's biggest lake, 4.5 miles with no traffic lights and almost no hills. It is where the city's runners go to do a steady long run, and one lap is a clean seven kilometres. Fog sits on it most mornings. Park on Lake Merced Boulevard and run it anticlockwise, so the lake is on your right.

items.title: The Embarcadero run
items.area: Pier 39 to Oracle Park along the water
items.hoursFrom: Port of San Francisco
items.source: Port of San Francisco

stops.text: Start at Pier 39 — sea lions on the docks
Past the Ferry Building clock tower
Under the Bay Bridge, by Rincon Park

items.why: Flat, wide and ten minutes from North Beach: the promenade along the piers from Pier 39 to the ballpark and back, about six and a half kilometres. Go before eight, while it is joggers and delivery trucks rather than crowds. On a Saturday, finish at the Ferry Building farmers' market.

items.title: Stanford Perimeter Trail
items.area: Around the Stanford campus, from Stanford Avenue or Junipero Serra
items.hoursFrom: Stanford University — public trail
items.source: Stanford Land, Buildings & Real Estate
items.why: A soft-surfaced trail on the edge of the campus, along Stanford Avenue and Junipero Serra, that most Palo Alto runners use because it is flat and shaded in places and there are no cars. It is about three and a half miles, and it joins the Dish loop if you want the hills. Run it in the evening, when the foothills catch the sun.

items.title: Lands End Coastal Trail
items.area: Lands End Lookout, 680 Point Lobos Ave · 3.4 mi loop · rolling, with stairs
items.hoursFrom: Golden Gate National Recreation Area; visitor centre 9 to 5
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy; AllTrails
items.why: The wild edge of the city: a cliff-top trail through cypress from the ruins of the Sutro Baths towards the Golden Gate, with shipwrecks below at low tide. Take the steps down to the stone labyrinth on the point and to Mile Rock Beach. The loop is about 3.4 miles with a few hundred steps. Start at the Lookout and finish with the sunset over the baths.

items.title: Mount Tam — East Peak
items.area: East Peak lot · 0.7 mi paved loop, then the Plank Trail to the lookout
items.hoursFrom: Mount Tamalpais State Park — 7am to sunset, gates locked after
items.source: California State Parks; AllTrails
items.why: The summit of the Bay without the climb: drive up Panoramic Highway to the East Peak lot and walk the Verna Dunshee loop, a flat, paved path round the top with the whole Bay, the Farallones and Mount Diablo in view. Then take the steps and the Plank Trail up to the Gardner fire lookout at the peak. Go in the afternoon, when fog often fills the valleys below you. Parking is $8, cash only.

items.title: Big Basin — the Redwood Loop
items.area: Park headquarters · 0.6 mi loop, or on to Sempervirens Falls · parking by reservation
items.hoursFrom: California State Parks — day use 8am to sunset, reservation encouraged
items.source: California State Parks; Reimagining Big Basin
items.why: California's oldest state park, which burned in the 2020 fire and is coming back. The old-growth giants around the headquarters survived. The Redwood Loop is a flat 0.6 miles past Mother of the Forest, and newly reopened trail goes on to Sempervirens Falls. Book parking online first. The long trails, Skyline-to-the-Sea included, are still closed, so do not plan on them.

items.title: Devil's Slide Trail
items.area: Between Pacifica and Montara · 1.3 mi each way · paved, bikes welcome
items.hoursFrom: San Mateo County Parks — opens at 8am, closes around sunset
items.source: San Mateo County Parks
items.why: A stretch of the old Highway 1 above the ocean, closed to cars when the tunnels opened in 2013 and now a paved path for walkers and bikes. It hangs on a cliff over the Pacific with seabirds nesting on the rocks below. It is flat enough for anyone and dramatic enough for everyone. Walk out to the old bunker lookout, and bring binoculars from December to April for grey whales.

items.title: Sharks and PWHL San Jose at SAP Center
items.area: SAP Center, downtown San Jose
items.hoursNote: Game nights, October to April — the schedule is the timetable
items.source: San Jose Sharks; PWHL
items.why: The Bay's hockey arena, called the Shark Tank, by the Caltrain station in downtown San Jose. The Sharks play here from October to April, and from December the PWHL's new San Jose team plays its first professional women's hockey here too. Take Caltrain to Diridon and walk across the road. The upper bowl is loud and cheap.

items.title: Earthquakes and Bay FC at PayPal Park
items.area: PayPal Park, by San Jose airport
items.hoursNote: Match days, March to November — the schedule is the timetable
items.source: San Jose Earthquakes; Bay FC
items.why: An 18,000-seat football stadium with the stands right on the pitch and the largest outdoor bar in North America behind one goal. The Earthquakes play MLS here and Bay FC, the women's NWSL side, plays here too, usually Saturday or Sunday afternoons. The Caltrain stop at Santa Clara is a short walk. Stand with the supporters' groups behind the goal if you want to sing.

items.title: Stanford volleyball and basketball at Maples
items.area: Maples Pavilion, Stanford campus
items.hoursNote: Volleyball September to November, basketball November to March — the schedule is the timetable
items.source: Stanford Athletics
items.why: Stanford's indoor arena, where the women's volleyball team, one of the most successful in the country, plays through the autumn, and both basketball teams play the winter. It seats about 7,000 and the student section makes it feel like more. Tickets are cheap next to anything professional. The Cal match sells out first.

items.title: Cal football at Memorial Stadium
items.area: California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley hills
items.hoursNote: Home games, September to November — the schedule is the timetable
items.source: Cal Athletics
items.why: A 1923 stadium set into Strawberry Canyon in the Berkeley hills, with the bay and the Golden Gate behind the west stands. Take BART to Downtown Berkeley and walk up through campus with everyone else. The game to go to is the Big Game against Stanford, which Cal hosts in even years.
